nodes.title: Coleman formula for an elliptic syntomic regulator
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite, p>2, and let X/O_K be a smooth proper elliptic model with generic fibre E. Fix a p-adic logarithm branch. Let u lie in K2(X)^(2) tensor Q, and let its restriction to K(E) have finite symbol presentation sum_i n_i{f_i,g_i}, n_i rational, with all horizontal tame symbols trivial. For every holomorphic differential eta on E, Tr(reg_syn(u) cup eta)=sum_i n_i sum_P ord_P(f_i) Tr_(K(P)/K)(CT_P(int log(g_i) eta)). Here CT is the log-free constant term of a Coleman primitive in a local parameter, computed after finite extension; it is parameter independent for this primitive, and the degree-zero divisor makes the sum independent of its additive constant. This formula specialises the D.5 symbol comparison to elliptic symbols and their E.7 certificates. It determines the pairing with holomorphic eta, not the whole two-dimensional de Rham regulator vector.
hypotheses: K is a finite p-adic field; E has the stated smooth proper good-reduction model.
The weight-two regulator, cup/trace pairing and restriction come from PadicHodgeRegulators:D.5; the model class must be supplied, not postulated.
Coleman primitives must admit the stated expansions; general elliptic pullback and finite-extension descent inherit the supplier hypothesis/gap.
proofSteps: Import the actual D.5 regulator and cup/trace comparison and the E.6 good-reduction extension of rational unramified classes.

Specialise Besser–de Jeu Remark 1.10 to E. Write log(g)=m log(t)+analytic and eta=analytic dt: integration of t^n log(t) has a t^(n+1) factor, so changing the parameter does not change the constant term.
Use Coleman L1 for integration, Galois equivariance and finite-extension descent. For closed points use residue-field trace, not one chosen conjugate value.
Use the D.5 symbol formula to descend through Steinberg relations and presentation changes; local expansion alone is not that proof. Sum ord_P(f)[K(P):K]=0 to remove the primitive constant.

sources.match: Public restatement of the K2 Coleman–de Shalit formula, with the constant-term and closed-point conventions on pp. 3–4; no K4 theorem is imported.

acceptance: Changing a primitive by a constant does not change a principal-divisor evaluation.
For a degree-two point, both conjugate evaluations enter via the residue-field trace.
On P1 the Steinberg symbol {z,1-z} is zero; its proper-curve syntomic regulator is zero, although a based dilogarithm primitive on the punctured line need not vanish.
The same corrected symbol can be presented in two ways without changing this pairing.

nodes.title: Frobenius correction in the elliptic regulator comparison
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good reduction at p>2. Extend its Q_p-linear untwisted crystalline Frobenius and cup pairing from H_dR^1(E/Q_p) to a coefficient field K containing gamma. Under the D.5 identification of the weight-two syntomic regulator target with this extended de Rham space, let Phi be that extended linear operator, and let z=log_BK(reg_et(u)). Then reg_syn(u)=(1-p^(-2)Phi)z. With B(a,b)=Tr(a cup b), B(Phi a,Phi b)=p B(a,b). For Phi v=gamma v, gamma nonzero, B(reg_syn(u),v)=(1-1/(p gamma)) B(z,v). Consequently the scalar normalised in this packet is (1-p/gamma)(1-1/(p gamma)) B(z,v)/B(omega,v), with B(omega,v) nonzero. The two factors have different origins and neither is omitted.
hypotheses: E is defined over Q and p>2 is a good prime; K is a coefficient extension containing the selected eigenvalue. This is not an assertion of K-linearity for the semilinear crystalline Frobenius of an arbitrary curve over K.
Use the untwisted H_dR^1 Frobenius (eigenpolynomial X²-a_p X+p); the Tate twist has already been accounted for in p^(-2).
The étale regulator and Bloch–Kato logarithm and their domains are supplied by D.5/D.2.
proofSteps: Import the cohomological identity from D.5, with the convention recorded in Asakura–Chida footnote 10 (Besser Proposition 9.11).
From Frobenius similitude and Phi v=gamma v obtain B(Phi z,v)=p/gamma B(z,v).
Expand B((1-p^(-2)Phi)z,v). Apply the scalar definition for the second displayed expression.

sources.match: States the identity (1-p^(-2)Phi)log(reg_f)=reg_syn and its eigenvector pairing.
The published preview independently confirms the correction identity; its body was not read.

nodes.title: The Frobenius-normalised weight-two regulator scalar
nodes.statement: For a characteristic-zero coefficient field K, a K-vector space H, a K-bilinear pairing B, omega,v,r in H and p,gamma in K, define frobeniusRegulatorScalar(p,gamma,B,omega,v,r)=(1-p/gamma) B(r,v)/B(omega,v). The coordinate formula is total, but its geometric use requires gamma nonzero and B(omega,v) nonzero. In the elliptic case H=H_dR^1(E/K), B=Tr(cup), r=reg_syn(xi), omega is the selected Néron differential and Phi v=gamma v. It is linear in r, invariant under multiplying v by a nonzero scalar, and scales by c^(-1) when omega is multiplied by c. At n=0 Gamma*(-n)=1.
hypotheses: Geometric use has p>2, p not dividing the conductor, gamma a selected root of X²-a_p X+p, v nonzero in its eigenspace, and Phi(omega) not equal to gamma omega.
For the algebraic definition the geometric types are not assumed or reconstructed; denominator nonvanishing is explicit in its API.
proofSteps: Use the n=0 definition of Rp,gamma in Asakura–Chida §3.4.
Instantiate the existing bilinear-form interface. Derive linearity and scaling by bilinearity and cancellation with nonzero denominators.
Keep the denominator guard as part of every geometric invocation; field division at zero is not an admissible period coordinate.

nodes.title: Néron periods and the weight-two refined L-function
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have conductor N, p>2 with p not dividing N, omega a Néron differential, and primitive integral cycles u+ and u- in the conjugation eigenspaces oriented by Omega+=int_(u+)omega>0 and Omega-/i>0. Let f_E be its newform and gamma a root of X²-a_p X+p with slope<1, or slope=1 with the refinement not theta-critical. Select the L1 period bases by the exact symbols lambda±(a,m)=pi i/Omega± times (int_infty^(a/m) f_gamma dz ± int_infty^(-a/m) f_gamma dz). Import the resulting L2 (or L3) eigen-distribution mu_gamma, and set Lp(E,chi,s)=int chi(x)<x>^(s-1)dmu_gamma. For tau(chi)=sum chi(a)exp(2pi i a/p^nu) and L(E,chi,s)=sum chi(n)a_n n^(-s), a nontrivial primitive chi has Lp(E,chi,1)=gamma^(-nu)tau(chi)L(E,chi^(-1),1)/Omega^(chi(-1)). The trivial character has (1-gamma^(-1))²L(E,1)/Omega+. Lp(E,omega_Teich^(-1),0) is the inverse-x moment, not a classical interpolation value. At critical slope use the eigenlift, not uniqueness from classical moments.
hypotheses: The periods belong to primitive cycles; the whole real locus can have index two and is not silently substituted.
The owner period-line basis must be matched to the specified Néron symbols; the pullback differential factor of a modular parametrisation must be included when used.
The character convention is the reviewed L1/L2 convention. E29 corrects the accepted-manuscript formula in its displayed finite-coset convention.
proofSteps: Import the L1 period lines and twisted Mellin formula, and the L2 p-adic distribution and interpolation theorem.
At weight two put j=0 in the owner moment formula; the stabilisation supplies the second Euler factor when chi is trivial.
For slope one import L3 non-theta-critical-lift and critical-slope-interpolation. Classical interpolation alone does not determine this distribution.
Track differential rescaling in both the periods and the regulator coordinate. Use L4 euler-factor-comparison as the explicit good-prime two-factor cross-check.

sources.match: The Néron periods and weight-two specialisation; interpolation uses the corrected reviewed supplier convention.
Explains why the theta-critical refinement is excluded.

acceptance: At chi=1 the Euler factor is the square (1-1/gamma)².
For primitive chi of conductor p^nu the factor is gamma^(-nu), and its complex twist is chi^(-1).
Replacing omega by c omega rescales Lp and Rp by c^(-1).
The CM split critical refinement does not satisfy the stated non-theta-critical hypothesis.
For the odd quadratic character modulo 3, tau²=-3, so 3/tau=-tau; this detects the accepted-manuscript sign error that even quadratic characters miss.

nodes.title: The common rational-scalar Beilinson relation
nodes.statement: Let M be a Q-vector space (geometrically, the arithmetic-integral weight-two motivic group), K a characteristic-zero field, r_infty:M to R and r_p:M to K linear over Q, and A in R, B in K. Define WeightTwoBeilinsonRelation(r_infty,r_p,A,B) to mean: there exist xi in M, q in Q and epsilon in {1,-1} such that xi,q,r_infty(xi),r_p(xi) are nonzero, A=q r_infty(xi), and B=epsilon q r_p(xi), with q embedded separately in R and K. This is an explicit predicate on supplied maps; it neither constructs the motivic group nor asserts the conjecture. The ratios then equal q and epsilon q respectively. A common rational scalar is not an equality between elements of R and Q_p.
hypotheses: The geometric r_infty uses reg_D(xi)(u-)/(2pi i), and r_p uses frobeniusRegulatorScalar with actual syntomic regulator.
The group M is the integral part, not the whole unramified generic-fibre group.
Both regulator values and q are nonzero; no division-by-zero convention can make the relation hold.
proofSteps: At n=0 cross-multiply the ratio in Asakura–Chida Conjecture 3.3 with nonzero regulators.
Retain the rationality of the real ratio as its Beilinson component rather than comparing the two coefficient fields.
Use Q-linearity to transport witnesses under nonzero rational scaling.

nodes.title: Weight-two p-adic Beilinson conjecture for elliptic curves
nodes.statement: Conjecture, not a proved theorem: let E/Q have good reduction at p>2, fix Néron omega and oriented primitive cycles as in neron-refinement-period-dictionary, and select gamma with slope<1 or slope=1 non-theta-critical. Assume Phi(omega) is not gamma omega. Put M=H_M^2(E,Q(2))_Z, r_infty(xi)=reg_D(xi)(u-)/(2pi i), r_p(xi)=(1-p/gamma)Tr(reg_syn(xi) cup v_gamma)/Tr(omega cup v_gamma), A=Lprime(E,0) and B=Lp(E,omega_Teich^(-1),0). The conjecture asserts WeightTwoBeilinsonRelation(r_infty,r_p,A,B). In a concrete example a proposed witness needs both an arithmetic-integral certificate and an exact L-value comparison; numerical agreement is an acceptance diagnostic, not a proof.
hypotheses: All slope, good-reduction, orientation and denominator hypotheses of the normalisation nodes.
The rationality of A/r_infty is the real Beilinson component; the source p-adic ratio statement alone must not be read as a proof of it.
The L-function uses the exact finite-coset dictionary in this packet, including the version-scoped source corrections E28–E29.
proofSteps: Import the integral part from E.6, the Deligne comparison from ER.2 and the syntomic map from D.5.
Specialise Asakura–Chida Conjecture 3.3 to n=0 and their preceding real rationality formulation.
Apply the two normalisation nodes and the relation predicate. Retain conjectural status throughout.

sources.match: Pins the integral motivic witness, slope alternatives and the ratio; the predicate also records the real Beilinson rationality component.

acceptance: Its label remains conjecture even when a numerical example passes.
A horizontally unramified class with a nonzero vertical residue is not accepted as a witness.
A CM split theta-critical refinement is not accepted by this statement.

nodes.title: Full six-torsion certificate for the CM class on 36a1
nodes.statement: Let E:y²=x³+1, kappa=Q(sqrt(-3)), tau=(1+sqrt(-3))/2 and L=kappa(E[6]). In L(E) put psi6=6xy(x³+4)(x³-8)(x^9+228x^6+48x³+64) and rho=1/psi6, so div(rho)=35[O]-sum_(b in E[6],b not O)[b]. For every nonzero b in E[6], let f_b be the leading-coefficient-one Miller function with div(f_b)=6[b]-6[O], using t_O=-x/y. It is computed by the fixed chain 1,2,3,6: f_1=1, f_2=h_(b,b)/v_(2b), f_3=f_2 h_(2b,b)/v_(3b), f_6=f_3² h_(3b,3b)/v_(6b), normalised at O; v_O=1; h_(P,Q)=v_P when P+Q=O with P,Q nonzero, h_(O,P)=h_(P,O)=v_P and h_(O,O)=1, so the quotient h_(P,Q)/v_(P+Q) is one if an input is O. For each chosen a, put c_(a,b)=tame_b{rho,f_a}. For finite b not a this is f_a(b); at a it is r_a^6 u_a, where r_a and u_a are the leading units of rho and f_a in the specified local parameter; at O it is 6^6. Set S_a=(6{rho,f_a}+sum_(b not O){f_b,c_(a,b)})/6. Each numerator has tame value one at every point, including O. For ER.5 the three a are the images under the fixed CM uniformisation of 1/6,(5+4tau)/6,(3+2tau)/6. Sum these S_a, then descend by N/[L:Q], to obtain exactly ER.5 U in rational K2.
hypotheses: L contains all six-torsion points; the quadratic field alone does not suffice.
The leading coefficient at O is one for f_b; rho has leading coefficient -1/6 there. At finite b take t_b=x-x_b if y_b is nonzero, and t_b=y if y_b=0.
The uniformisation and character are exactly those of ER.1/ER.5; their algebraic-coordinate dictionary is a supplier request.
The generic-fibre certificate asserts no arithmetic integrality.
proofSteps: Evaluate the pinned division-polynomial recurrence at E to obtain the displayed psi6. Use the baseline torsion-zero equivalence, and check the factors have simple zeros on the curve; the pole order is 35.

Use the pinned existence of principal torsion divisors and the E.7 Miller-function construction. The fixed chain, including vertical/infinity conventions, makes every f_b explicit from its coordinates.
Use orders (-1,0) at b not a, (-1,6) at a and (35,-6) at O to obtain the stated leading-unit residues.

At b not O the corrected numerator has residue c_(a,b)^6 c_(a,b)^(-6)=1; outside E[6] it is 1. At O reciprocity over the fully split field gives c_(a,O) product_(b not O)c_(a,b)=1, hence the numerator residue is 1.
Invoke E.7 choice independence over a number field and rational descent to match ER.5 U. The schema specifies all 35 finite rows for each of the three a, rather than omitting nonrational rows.

nodes.title: The corrected CM L-value identity on 36a1
nodes.statement: For the preceding U on E:y²=x³+1, use ER.5 f=2sqrt(-3), g=-sqrt(-3), C=6, y²=(Im tau)²=3/4 and the corrected Fourier transform with kernel <dual,input>. The reviewed character evaluation is chi_hat(gbar)g=3. Therefore L(E,2)=pi/(324 i) R_q(U)=(2pi/3) sum_(a in the three ER.5 index points)D_E(a), where R_q(U)=i 6³ sum_a D_E(a). There is no additional factor |mu_kappa|=6. The parent numerical check L(E,2)=0.94001300738822578150… and Lprime(E,0)=0.85718907492991773072… remains a diagnostic. Reducing this sum to the parent empirical identity -(2pi/3)D_E((2,3)) requires the explicit point/distribution identity and is recorded as a gap rather than inferred from decimal agreement.
hypotheses: Use the twist-sensitive Hecke character of this rational model and ER.5 equality with the full elliptic Euler product.
The regulator is Bloch R_q=J_q+iD_q in the reviewed convention; translating to the Beilinson period coordinate requires ER.2.
No p-adic L-value theorem for U is inferred from this complex formula.
proofSteps: Import ER.5 the CM setup, class U, Fourier transform and corrected L-value theorem, including inherited E7–E9.
Substitute C=6, y²=3/4 and chi_hat(gbar)g=3 into pi chi_hat(gbar)g/(i y² C⁴), obtaining pi/(324i).
Use ER.4 R_q(S_a)=C³R_q(a) and the real-valued L-series to remove the J-sum.
Keep the one-point numerical identity separate until the supplier point/distribution dictionary supplies an exact proof.

nodes.title: An explicit corrected symbol at a quadratic six-torsion point
nodes.statement: Let L=Q(zeta), zeta²+zeta+1=0, E:y²=x³+1, T=(2zeta,3), A=(0,1), B=(0,-1). Then 2T=A,3T=(-zeta,0),6T=O and B=-A. Put ell=y-2zeta²x+1, m=y-zeta²x-1, fT=ell²m²/((zeta²x)²(zeta²x+1)), fA=(y-1)² and fB=(y+1)². These have divisors div(ell)=2[T]+[B]-3[O], div(x)=[A]+[B]-2[O], div(fT)=6[T]-6[O], div(fA)=6[A]-6[O], div(fB)=6[B]-6[O]. Set cT=1/(4zeta²), cA=2, cB=2zeta² and beta=6{ell,x}+{fT,cT}+{fA,cA}+{fB,cB}. With tame{f,g}=(-1)^(ord f ord g)(f^(ord g)/g^(ord f))(P), the uncorrected symbol has values cT,cA,cB,1 at T,A,B,O. The corrected beta has value one at every place. It defines a class in K2T(E_L), hence a unique rational K2(E_L) lift by E.3. Its raw representative quadraticSymbol is an element of the existing free abelian group on pairs of units; the symbol quotient and certificate are imported. Its support is the subset {T,A,B,O} of the parent target support.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero; the selected complex embedding has zeta=exp(2pi i/3).
Use the same E.7 symbol certificate and tame convention as the parent.
Unramifiedness is horizontal. A global arithmetic-integral certificate is a separate E.6/E.7 obligation.
proofSteps: Substitute the tangent line into the curve: (2zeta²x-1)²-x³-1=-x(x-2zeta)²; the secant gives -x(x-2zeta)(x+zeta). Together with div(x), these prove the displayed divisors and fT.
At T use x-2zeta, at A and B use x, and at O use -x/y. At B ell/x has leading value -2zeta², so the tame sign gives +2zeta².
Compute cT cA cB=1. At each finite support point the residue is c^6 c^(-6)=1. At O the correction residues multiply to (cT cA cB)^6=1; outside the support all entries are units.
Apply E.7 symbol-certificates and the E.3 rational lift. Keep the raw free-group expansion as a prototype until the supplier quotient exists.

nodes.title: Quadratic transfer and its degree-two residue certificate
nodes.statement: For beta above, let beta_bar be its zeta-to-zeta² conjugate. In K2(Q(E)) tensor Q the transfer N_(L/Q)beta equals gamma=6{H,x}+{F,1/4}+{fA,4}+{fB,4}, where H=(y+1)²+2x(y+1)+4x²=ell ell_bar, J=(y-1)²+x(y-1)+x²=m m_bar, and F=H²J²/[x^4(x²-x+1)]=fT fT_bar. This is a rational identity: rewriting cT=zeta/4 and cB=2zeta² discards symbols with a root-of-unity entry, killed by 3. At the Q-closed point Z=(x²+2x+4=0,y=3), with x0=2zeta, the tame value of {H,x} is 1/x0²=1/(4zeta²) in Q(zeta), not its norm 1/16. Its value to the sixth power is (1/4)^6 and cancels {F,1/4}. At A and B the uncorrected value is 4 and cancels the corresponding order-six correction. At O the value of the corrected expression is (1/4)^12 4^6 4^6=1. Thus gamma has an exact horizontal certificate over Q; the integral transfer N beta itself is certified by E.7 transfer-of-certified-classes. No equality of these integral representatives is asserted.
hypotheses: L/Q is the actual quadratic constant-field extension; residue-field norms are taken only in the transfer boundary formula.
The rational representative discards 3-torsion and is not an integral formula for N beta.
proofSteps: Apply the E.7 projection formula to the terms with second entry in Q. For the others use bilinearity and the root-of-unity torsion before tensoring with Q.
Compute H,J,F exactly using zeta²+zeta+1=0 and y²=x³+1.
Compute div(H)=2[T]+2[Tbar]+2[B]-6[O] and div(F)=6[T]+6[Tbar]-12[O]. At Z use x-x0 over its own residue field and compute 1/x0².
Check the remaining A,B,O rows directly and compare them with the E.7 norm-residue formula. The result is the full certificate, not just the normed-product reciprocity check.

nodes.title: Regulator trace of the explicit quadratic class
nodes.statement: Use ER.4 diamond (f) diamond (g)=sum m_P n_Q[Q-P] and R_q=J_q+iD_q, with r_source(xi)(dz)=one half conjugate R_q(diamond xi). For ell and x the diamond is 7[O]+2[T]-5[2T]+2[3T]-2[4T]-4[5T]. Since 2T=A,4T=-A,5T=-T and 3T is two-torsion, its odd evaluation is 6R_q(T)-3R_q(A). Constant-entry corrections have zero regulator, so r_source(beta)(dz)=18 conjugate R_q(T)-9 conjugate R_q(A). The transfer trace is r_source(N beta)(dz)=18 conjugate(R_q(T)+R_q(Tbar)-R_q(A)). For the rational transferred class and the real-adapted differential its real part vanishes, hence r_source(N beta)(dz)=-18i(D_E(T)+D_E(Tbar)-D_E(A)). Neither the individual beta regulator nor the trace is identified with the Néron-cycle R_infty without the ER.2 factor-two and period conversion.
hypotheses: Use the parent ER.1 orientation and ER.3 odd q-invariant function.
T and Tbar correspond to the two embeddings of L; A is rational.
The full complex identity precedes the imaginary-coordinate simplification.

Apply ER.4 divisor formula; all constant-symbol corrections contribute zero.
Apply the existing constant-field trace theorem, then the rational real-structure comparison to obtain the imaginary expression.
Convert to the Deligne period only through ER.2. Parent decimals for D(T),D(Tbar) are diagnostics and do not prove a distribution identity or a p-adic L-value equality.

nodes.title: Arithmetic integrality and admissibility of the worked examples
nodes.statement: On E11:y²+y=x³-x² (11a3), import xi={x,y}+{-1,x}, its rational lift and its arithmetic-integral certificate on the regular minimal proper model over Z. The discriminant is -11; the fibre at 11 is split I1 and irreducible, and x,y have vertical order zero. Thus xi is an admissible integral input at every good p>2 with p not equal to 11, after the eigenline and period conditions above. Its complex source regulator is -11i/(8pi)L(E11,2)=-pi i/2 Lprime(E11,0), with the parent orientation. In contrast the u=1/3 example y²=x(x+1)(x+1/9) has the vertical residue 1/w of infinite order on the component V=0 at 3 of the E.8 model, so no nonzero rational multiple of its horizontally certified class lies in the global integral part. A regulator can be evaluated locally at a good prime without making that second class an integral witness for the global Beilinson conjecture. The quadratic beta and CM U need an independent vertical certificate for any global integral claim.
hypotheses: The arithmetic model, integral part and vertical boundary maps are owned by E.6, and their certificate by E.7/E.8.
The E11 real regulator is r_source, not directly the Deligne cycle coordinate.
No p-adic numerical L-value comparison for E11, beta or U is asserted.
proofSteps: Import both sides of the parent integrality example and E.8 worked-example-bad-fibre.
Apply E.6 vertical-residues and E.7 integral-certificates to the irreducible E11 fibres, whose x,y valuations vanish.
At good p obtain the local smooth proper model and invoke the pairing and scalar contracts, checking the selected refinement.
For the negative example retain the nonzero infinite-order vertical residue, even though its horizontal certificate and reciprocity tests pass.

sourceIssues.reason: Sum the displayed alpha^(-nu)lambda^±(a,p^nu) masses against chi(a). The sign-part gives 2pi i/Omega times sum chi(a)int_infty^(a/p^nu)f_gamma(z)dz, whose finite Fourier transform is tau(chi)L(f_gamma,chi^(-1),1)/Omega. The primitive p-power twist removes the stabilisation term. Already for the odd quadratic character modulo 3, tau=exp(2pi i/3)-exp(4pi i/3), tau²=-3, so 3/tau=-tau: the printed and derived factors have opposite signs regardless of whether a twist uses chi or chi^(-1), which coincide here. The reviewed L1/L2 owner independently gives the derived formula. Even quadratic tests conceal the error.
